name: Propp Machine grammar
note: Function labels follow Propp's Morphology of the Folktale (1928; Eng. tr. 1958/1968). All glosses and variant descriptions are paraphrased in our own words. Variant lists are abridged.

functions.name: Initial situation
functions.gloss: The family or the hero is introduced; not a function proper.
variants: future hero introduced by name or status

functions.name: Absentation
functions.gloss: Someone in the family goes away.
variants: the young ones go out to walk or work

functions.name: Interdiction
functions.gloss: A prohibition (or, inverted, an order) is laid on the hero.

functions.name: Violation
functions.gloss: The prohibition is broken (or the order carried out).

functions.name: Reconnaissance
functions.gloss: The villain tries to find something out.
variants: villain seeks the whereabouts of a child or treasure
the hero's side questions the villain (inverted form)

functions.name: Delivery
functions.gloss: The villain learns what he wanted to know.
variants: information gained by observation or careless talk

functions.name: Trickery
functions.gloss: The villain deceives the victim in order to take possession.

functions.name: Complicity
functions.gloss: The victim is taken in and unwittingly helps the enemy.

functions.name: Villainy
functions.gloss: The villain harms or injures a member of the family. The tale's motor.
variants: seizes a magical agent or helper
steals light or a heavenly body

functions.name: Lack
functions.gloss: A family member lacks or desires something (a bride, a wonder, a means of life).
variants: lack of the means of life

functions.name: Mediation
functions.gloss: The misfortune is made known; the hero is asked, sent, or allowed to go.

functions.name: Beginning counteraction
functions.gloss: The seeker agrees to, or decides on, counteraction.

functions.name: Departure
functions.gloss: The hero leaves home.

functions.name: First function of the donor
functions.gloss: The hero is tested, questioned, or attacked, preparing the way for a magical agent or helper.
variants: a dying or dead person's request
a captive begs to be freed
a hostile creature tries to destroy the hero

functions.name: Hero's reaction
functions.gloss: The hero responds to the donor, well or badly.
variants: answers the greeting politely or rudely

functions.name: Receipt of a magical agent
functions.gloss: The hero acquires the use of a magical agent or helper.

functions.name: Guidance
functions.gloss: The hero is transferred, delivered, or led to the whereabouts of the object of search.
variants: travels on the ground or water
uses a fixed means such as a stair or bridge

functions.name: Struggle
functions.gloss: Hero and villain join in direct combat or contest.
variants: a game of cards or chance

functions.name: Branding
functions.gloss: The hero is marked.
variants: a wound or mark on the body

functions.name: Victory
functions.gloss: The villain is defeated.

functions.name: Liquidation
functions.gloss: The initial misfortune or lack is set right. The tale's peak.
variants: obtained by several helpers at once

functions.name: Return
functions.gloss: The hero returns.

functions.name: Pursuit
functions.gloss: The hero is chased.

functions.name: Rescue
functions.gloss: The hero is saved from pursuit.

functions.name: Unrecognized arrival
functions.gloss: The hero, unrecognized, arrives home or in another country.

functions.name: Unfounded claims
functions.gloss: A false hero presents unfounded claims.

functions.name: Difficult task
functions.gloss: A difficult task is proposed to the hero.

functions.name: Solution
functions.gloss: The task is resolved.

functions.name: Recognition
functions.gloss: The hero is recognized.

functions.name: Exposure
functions.gloss: The false hero or villain is exposed.

functions.name: Transfiguration
functions.gloss: The hero is given a new appearance.
variants: new appearance by a helper's magic

functions.name: Punishment
functions.gloss: The villain or false hero is punished (or pardoned).

functions.name: Wedding
functions.gloss: The hero is married and/or ascends the throne.
variants: a reward instead of a wedding

functions.name: Unidentified element
functions.gloss: An episode we could not assign to any of Propp's functions (annotation marker; not a Propp function).

roles.name: Donor (provider)
roles.propp: preparation for and transmission of the magical agent

roles.name: Princess (sought-for person) and her father
roles.propp: assigning tasks, branding, exposure, recognition, punishment, wedding

roles.name: Hero (seeker or victim)
roles.propp: departure, reaction to the donor, wedding

roles.name: False hero
roles.propp: departure, negative reaction to the donor, unfounded claims

openers.why: An interdiction is paired with its violation.
Reconnaissance is paired with delivery of information.
Villainy must be liquidated within its move.
A lack must be liquidated within its move.
A difficult task is paired with its solution.
Unfounded claims are paired with exposure.

requires.why: Liquidation presupposes a villainy or lack.
The hero reacts to a donor's action.
The magical agent normally follows the donor episode.
Recognition is by a mark or by a solved task.

refinements.what: Functions marked implicit (narrated offstage or fused with another act) count as present.
refinements.basis: Propp on assimilation and fusion of functions; Finlayson's annotation practice of implicit functions.

refinements.what: A backward jump is allowed when it re-enters a repeatable function already performed in the same move (trebling or repetition of an episode).
refinements.basis: Propp on trebling; Dundes on motifeme sequences.

refinements.what: The difficult task and its solution (M, N) may stand anywhere after the complication.
refinements.basis: Propp's remarks that some functions (notably the task) are mobile; Meletinsky et al. on the task as a variable block.

refinements.what: The donor block (D, E, F) may precede the complication.
refinements.basis: Propp's note on the transposition of the donor episode.

refinements.what: Reconnaissance, delivery, trickery and complicity may follow the villainy when carried out by the hero's side.
refinements.basis: Propp on the inverted forms of ε and η.

refinements.what: An interdiction, reconnaissance, or trickery need not be followed by its partner.
refinements.basis: Bremond (1966): every opening function may stay virtual.

refinements.what: A magical agent or helper may appear without a donor episode; recognition may occur without a mark.
refinements.basis: Propp lists agents that appear of their own accord, and recognition after long absence.

refinements.what: Up to 20% of entries may be unidentified (X).
refinements.basis: Dundes on allomotifs; tellers add episodes that a function inventory does not cover.
